html:
The Sahtu Dene are a First Nations people of the area around Great Bear Lake and the Mackenzie River in Canada's Northwest Territories. Sahtú is their name for the lake. They speak North Slavey, an Athabaskan language, and were once called the Hare Indians, after the snowshoe hares they hunted.

They lived in small, mobile family groups, hunting caribou and moose, snaring hares and fishing the lakes, a typical life of the subarctic forest. Alexander Mackenzie came down the river in 1789, and fur trade posts such as Fort Good Hope followed in the early 1800s, later run by the Hudson's Bay Company.

Oil was found at Norman Wells in their land in the 1920s. In 1993 the Sahtu Dene and Métis signed a land claim agreement with Canada. See also Sahtu Dene and Métis on the modern map.
